source.reflectsPeriod: 2025-2026 rules (no dated instances; rules are stable across years)
source.basis: US Code 5 USC 6103 (federal holidays), NIST/US DOT daylight-saving rules (Uniform Time Act as amended 2005), typical K-12 and college academic calendars from state/district and university catalogs as recalled, BLS National Compensation Survey for paid-holiday prevalence, FLSA and FMCSA hours rules.

values.doc: The school-year section as in the source: windows, daily hours, breaks, terms.

instructional_days.note: Most states require 175-180 days; some set hours instead of days.

start_window_by_region.Northeast: Aug 28-Sep 8 (after Labor Day in NY/NJ/New England)

breaks.name: Thanksgiving break
breaks.when: Wednesday before Thanksgiving through the Friday after (a full week in some Southern districts)

breaks.name: Presidents' Day or mid-winter break
breaks.when: third Monday of February; a full week in the Northeast

breaks.name: Spring break
breaks.when: one week between early March and mid-April (often near Easter)

values.note: School year start/end shown as windows; the engine should pick a consistent date per region.

spring.classes_begin_window: Jan 12-Jan 25 (often the week of MLK Day)

quarter_system.note: Used by a minority of colleges (e.g. several UC and Pacific Northwest schools).
